about.h1: The Quran is Allah’s guidance for humanity, showing a clear way to live with faith, justice, mercy, and accountability.
about.lede: AskQuran helps people reach Quranic guidance clearly, directly, and with proper context — never an invented answer, always the source text.
about.whyHead: The Quran is guidance for human life
about.whyP1: It speaks to the heart, the family, society, business, justice, mercy, accountability, and the relationship between a person and Allah. It teaches people how to worship, how to deal with others, how to protect the rights of parents, spouses, children, relatives, orphans, the poor, and the vulnerable — and how to live with honesty, patience, dignity, and responsibility.
about.whyP2: It gives clear guidance on many matters people face in daily life: inheritance, marriage, divorce, wealth, trade, debt, charity, oppression, forgiveness, repentance, and personal conduct. It tells the stories of prophets and earlier nations — not only as history, but as lessons about belief, arrogance, injustice, corruption, morality, and the consequences of human choices.
about.beliefLead: AskQuran is built around this belief:
about.beliefHi: people should be able to reach Quranic guidance clearly, directly, and with proper context.
about.whatP1: When someone asks a life-related question, AskQuran searches the available Quran data and returns relevant Quran references — with the original Arabic ayah, a selected translation, surrounding ayah context, and tafsir where available.
about.inc1s: The Quran ayah in its original Arabic
about.inc4s: The verses immediately before and after
about.inc6s: Every text traced to its origin
about.lineHead: It points to the source — it does not speak for it
about.does1: Search indexed Quran data and return relevant references
about.does2: Quote the source text directly and in full context
about.does3: Help people study the relevant passages with clarity
about.does4: Say so plainly when no clear source-backed reference is found
about.doesNot1: Generate religious opinions, fatwas, or personal interpretations
about.doesNot3: Alter translations or tafsir in any way
about.doesNot4: Invent an answer or stretch relevance to fill a gap
about.sensitiveHead: Topic labels are a navigation layer — nothing more
about.sensitiveP1: For sensitive subjects such as inheritance, divorce, women's rights, family disputes, property, or social conduct, AskQuran uses reviewed topic metadata to connect common questions with relevant Quran passages.
about.noteH3: These labels are only a way to navigate
about.noteP: They are not Quran text, not tafsir, and not religious rulings. They must be reviewed before being used publicly, and they are kept clearly separate from the source text at every step.

about.pledge1s: The source ayah is kept exactly as revealed, untouched.
about.pledge2s: Presented as written by their named authors.
about.pledge3s: Source text and topic labels never blur together.
about.pledge4s: No clear reference? We say so, rather than stretch.

facts.animal.cowN: Mentioned in the account of the heifer in Surah Al-Baqarah.
facts.animal.calfN: Mostly refers to the calf taken for worship by the people of Musa.
facts.animal.camelN: Different terms are used, including the she-camel (نَاقَة) of Salih.
facts.animal.cattleN: The general term anʿām covers grazing livestock.
facts.animal.sheepGoatN: Listed among the pairs of grazing livestock.
facts.animal.dogN: Includes the dog of the companions of the cave.
facts.animal.wolfN: Mentioned in the account of Yusuf.
facts.animal.elephantN: Referenced in the account of the companions of the elephant.
facts.animal.snakeN: Different terms are used; some occur in the account of Musa's staff.
facts.animal.birdN: General references to birds across several contexts.
facts.animal.hoopoeN: Mentioned in the account of Sulayman.
facts.animal.crowN: Mentioned in the account of the two sons of Adam.
facts.animal.fishWhaleN: Includes the fish associated with Musa's journey and Yunus. Identification as fish or whale varies by translation.
facts.animal.beeN: Surah An-Nahl is named after the bee.
facts.animal.antN: Mentioned in the valley of the ants in the account of Sulayman.
facts.animal.spiderN: Referenced in a parable about frail reliance.
facts.animal.flyN: Mentioned in a parable about the powerlessness of false objects of worship.
facts.animal.mosquitoN: Mentioned as an example Allah may use, however small.
facts.animal.locustN: Mentioned among the signs sent to Pharaoh's people, and at the gathering.
facts.animal.liceN: Listed among the signs sent to Pharaoh's people.
facts.animal.frogN: Listed among the signs sent to Pharaoh's people.
facts.sign.starsN: Both 'star' (najm) and 'planet/heavenly body' (kawkab) terms are included.
facts.sign.mountainsN: Includes the term rawāsī (firm, anchoring mountains).
facts.sign.plantsN: General references to vegetation Allah causes to grow, including derived growth forms (e.g. fa-anbatnā, 'We caused to grow', in 80:27).
facts.sign.humanCreationN: References to the stages of human creation. Terms are shown cautiously; no modern scientific claim is made.

social.i.truthSpeech.label: The Quran commands being with the truthful and speaking straight.
social.i.greet.title: Return Greetings
social.i.greet.label: The Quran commands returning greetings with something equal or better.
social.i.noArrogance.title: No Arrogance
social.i.noArrogance.label: The Quran forbids arrogance and walking proudly on the earth.
social.i.noInsult.title: No Insulting Others
social.i.noInsult.label: The Quran forbids insulting those others revere as this leads to insults in return.
social.i.beGood.title: Be Good to Others
social.i.beGood.label: The Quran commands goodness to parents, relatives, neighbors, and all people.
relations.title: Relations with Non-Muslims
relations.subtitle: Quranic references on kindness, justice, treaties, and limits with non-Muslims.
relations.sourceNote: Relations references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. No generated political commentary.
relations.i.kindnessNonHostile.title: Kindness to Non-Hostile
relations.i.kindnessNonHostile.label: The Quran permits kindness and justice toward those who do not fight you for your faith.
relations.i.actJustly.title: Act Justly Toward All
relations.i.actJustly.label: The Quran commands being upholders of justice even toward those you dislike.
relations.i.noCompulsion.title: No Compulsion in Religion
relations.i.noCompulsion.label: The Quran declares there is no compulsion in religion.
relations.i.debateBest.title: Debate in the Best Way
relations.i.debateBest.label: The Quran commands inviting to Allah's way with wisdom and good argument.
relations.i.doNotAid.title: Do Not Aid Those Who Fight You
relations.i.doNotAid.label: The Quran forbids taking as allies those who fight believers and expel them.
relations.i.honorTreaties.title: Honor Treaties
relations.i.honorTreaties.label: The Quran commands fulfilling treaties with those who have not broken them.
relations.i.breakTreaty.title: Respond to Treaty Breaking
relations.i.breakTreaty.label: The Quran allows ending a treaty with those who break it.
relations.i.refugeSeeker.title: Grant Refuge to One Who Seeks It
relations.i.refugeSeeker.label: The Quran commands granting protection to a disbeliever who seeks refuge.
brotherhood.title: Brotherhood & Community
brotherhood.subtitle: Quranic references on Muslim unity, reconciliation, cooperation, and the ummah.
brotherhood.sourceNote: Brotherhood references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. No generated commentary.
brotherhood.i.believersBrothers.title: Believers Are Brothers
brotherhood.i.believersBrothers.label: The Quran declares all believers are brothers and commands reconciliation.
brotherhood.i.holdRope.title: Hold to Allah's Rope Together
brotherhood.i.holdRope.label: The Quran commands holding to the rope of Allah all together and not dividing.
brotherhood.i.doNotDivide.title: Do Not Divide
brotherhood.i.doNotDivide.label: The Quran condemns dividing into sects after clear guidance has come.
brotherhood.i.reconcileDispute.title: Reconcile Those in Dispute
brotherhood.i.reconcileDispute.label: The Quran commands making peace between two disputing groups of believers.
brotherhood.i.makeSettlement.title: Settlement Is Better
brotherhood.i.makeSettlement.label: The Quran favors reconciliation and settlement over prolonged dispute.
brotherhood.i.cooperateGood.title: Cooperate in Goodness
brotherhood.i.cooperateGood.label: The Quran commands cooperating in righteousness and taqwa, not in sin.
brotherhood.i.forbidEvil.title: Forbid Evil Together
brotherhood.i.forbidEvil.label: The Quran calls believers to command good and forbid evil together.
brotherhood.i.noEnmity.title: No Enmity Among Believers
brotherhood.i.noEnmity.label: The Quran forbids enmity between believers and asks forgiveness for all.
brotherhood.i.community.title: Best Community
brotherhood.i.community.label: The Quran describes the Muslim community as the best brought forth for mankind.
oaths.title: Oaths, Vows & Expiation
oaths.subtitle: Quranic references on oaths, their expiation, zihar, ila, and fulfilling vows.
oaths.sourceNote: Oaths references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. Legal application requires qualified scholarship.
oaths.i.doNotMakeObstacle.title: Do Not Make Oaths an Obstacle
oaths.i.doNotMakeObstacle.label: The Quran warns against using Allah's name as an excuse to avoid doing good.
oaths.i.laghwOath.title: Unintentional Oaths Overlooked
oaths.i.laghwOath.label: The Quran distinguishes unintentional oaths from deliberate ones.
oaths.i.oathExpiation.title: Expiation for Oaths
oaths.i.oathExpiation.label: The Quran prescribes expiation for breaking a deliberate oath.
oaths.i.expiateFeed.title: Feed Ten Poor People
oaths.i.expiateFeed.label: One form of expiation for oaths is feeding or clothing ten poor people.
oaths.i.expiateFasting.title: Fasting as Expiation
oaths.i.expiateFasting.label: If unable to do other expiation, fasting three days is prescribed.
oaths.i.ila.title: Ila — Oath of Abstention
oaths.i.ila.label: The Quran gives a four-month period for those who take an oath to abstain.
oaths.i.zihar.title: Zihar — Unlawful Comparison
oaths.i.zihar.label: The Quran addresses zihar and calls it an evil statement.
oaths.i.ziharExpiation.title: Expiation for Zihar
oaths.i.ziharExpiation.label: The Quran prescribes freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor for zihar.
oaths.i.fulfillVows.title: Fulfill Vows
oaths.i.fulfillVows.label: The Quran praises those who fulfill their vows and commands fulfilling them.
parents.i.orphans.title: Orphans
parents.i.orphans.label: The Quran commands kind treatment and protection of orphan property.
signs.title: Signs of Allah in Creation
signs.subtitle: Quranic verses pointing to the signs of Allah in the cosmos, earth, water, human self, and natural phenomena.
signs.sourceNote: Signs are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. AskQuran does not add scientific commentary or miracle claims.
signs.i.heavensEarth.title: Creation of the Heavens and Earth
signs.i.heavensEarth.label: The Quran repeatedly points to the creation of the heavens and earth as clear signs of Allah.
signs.i.dayNightAlternation.title: Alternation of Day and Night
signs.i.dayNightAlternation.label: The Quran presents the alternation of day and night as a sign for those who reflect.
signs.i.rainLife.title: Rain Giving Life to the Earth
signs.i.rainLife.label: Allah sends down rain and revives the dead earth — a Quranic sign of resurrection and mercy.
signs.i.creationHumans.title: Creation of the Human Being
signs.i.creationHumans.label: The Quran details human creation from humble origins as a sign of Allah's power.
signs.i.soulBreathed.title: The Soul and Sleep
signs.i.soulBreathed.label: Allah breathes the soul into the human form; sleep is described as a minor death.
signs.i.seasRivers.title: Seas, Rivers, and Ships
signs.i.seasRivers.label: The Quran points to the harnessing of seas and rivers as signs of divine provision.
signs.i.mountainsPegs.title: Mountains as Pegs
signs.i.mountainsPegs.label: The Quran describes mountains as pegs that stabilise the earth.
signs.i.starsNavigation.title: Stars as Navigation
signs.i.starsNavigation.label: The Quran describes stars as guides for those navigating land and sea.
signs.i.animalsSign.title: Animals as Signs
signs.i.animalsSign.label: The Quran points to cattle, bees, and animals as signs of Allah's provision and wisdom.
signs.i.windClouds.title: Wind and Clouds
signs.i.windClouds.label: The Quran describes winds as signs — carrying rain, driving ships, and scattering seeds.
women.title: Women in the Quran
women.subtitle: Quranic references on Maryam, Asiya, women in stories, spiritual equality, rights, and Ayesha cleared by revelation.
women.sourceNote: Women references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. No generated commentary.
women.i.maryamChosen.title: Maryam — Chosen and Purified
women.i.maryamChosen.label: The Quran states that Allah chose Maryam, purified her, and preferred her over all women of the worlds.
women.i.maryamAngel.title: The Angel Visits Maryam
women.i.maryamAngel.label: The Quran recounts the angel appearing to Maryam and the news of Isa's birth without a father.
women.i.maryamBirth.title: The Birth of Isa
women.i.maryamBirth.label: Maryam gave birth alone, and the Quran describes her patience, the miracle of the palm tree, and Isa speaking from the cradle.
women.i.maryamSurah.title: Surah Maryam — The Surah Named After Her
women.i.maryamSurah.label: Maryam is the only woman named in the Quran and the only woman to have a Surah named after her.
women.i.asiyaPrayer.title: Asiya's Prayer — A Model for Believers
women.i.asiyaPrayer.label: The Quran presents Asiya, wife of Pharaoh, as a model: she prayed for a house near Allah in Paradise.
women.i.queenSheba.title: The Queen of Sheba
women.i.queenSheba.label: The Quran recounts the Queen of Sheba's wisdom, her throne, and her submission to Allah.
women.i.wivesOfProphet.title: The Choice Given to the Prophet's Wives
women.i.wivesOfProphet.label: The Quran offered the Prophet's wives a choice between this world and Allah — they chose Allah.
women.i.ifkVerses.title: Ayesha Cleared by Revelation
women.i.ifkVerses.label: When Ayesha was falsely accused, Allah revealed verses directly clearing her name — among the clearest Quranic defences of any person.
women.i.equalBeliever.title: Believing Men and Women are Equal Before Allah
women.i.equalBeliever.label: The Quran explicitly lists believing men and women side by side as equal recipients of Allah's reward.
women.i.mothersHonour.title: The Honour of Mothers
women.i.mothersHonour.label: The Quran commands kindness to parents with special weight given to mothers, who bear hardship upon hardship.
women.i.womenRights.title: Women's Rights in the Quran
women.i.womenRights.label: The Quran establishes rights for women in marriage, maintenance, inheritance, and personal autonomy.
lineage.title: Faith Cannot Be Inherited
lineage.subtitle: The Quran is explicit: being related to a prophet does not guarantee salvation. Faith is individual — every soul is accountable only for its own choices.
lineage.sourceNote: References are drawn directly from Quran ayahs only. No added commentary beyond what the text states.
lineage.cat.wives: Wives Not Saved by Their Husbands
lineage.i.nuhSon.title: Nuh's Son — 'He is Not of Your Family'
lineage.i.nuhSon.label: Nuh called his son to board the ark. He refused and drowned. When Nuh pleaded, Allah answered: 'He is not of your family — his deeds were not righteous.' The clearest Quranic statement that lineage means nothing before Allah.
lineage.i.ibrahimFather.title: Ibrahim's Father — The Prophet Could Not Save Him
lineage.i.ibrahimFather.label: Ibrahim's father Azar was an idol-maker. Ibrahim prayed for him with tenderness, but after it became clear his father died in disbelief, Allah commanded Ibrahim to stop — and Ibrahim disassociated. Being the father of the greatest monotheist availed Azar nothing.
lineage.i.abuLahab.title: Abu Lahab — The Prophet's Uncle Condemned by Name
lineage.i.abuLahab.label: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's own uncle. He is the only person condemned to the Fire by name in the Quran. Surah Al-Masad declares his wealth and children will not avail him — he will enter a fire of blazing flame.
lineage.i.nuhWife.title: The Wife of Nuh — A Warning for Disbelievers
lineage.i.nuhWife.label: The Quran presents the wife of Nuh as one of two examples for disbelievers — she was married to a prophet yet betrayed him. Her closeness to a prophet did not save her. It was said to her: 'Enter the Fire with those who enter.'
lineage.i.lutWife.title: The Wife of Lut — Left Behind with the Destroyed
lineage.i.lutWife.label: The wife of Lut was told to leave with her husband but was among those destroyed. The Quran pairs her with the wife of Nuh as a deliberate dual example: two women married to prophets, both condemned because of their own choices.
lineage.i.abuLahabWife.title: The Wife of Abu Lahab — She Too Will Enter the Fire
lineage.i.abuLahabWife.label: The Quran condemns not only Abu Lahab but his wife alongside him — she carried thorns to harm the Prophet. Being the wife of the Prophet's uncle gave her no protection. She will carry wood as fuel with a rope of twisted fibre around her neck.
lineage.i.asiyaContrast.title: Asiya — Wife of the Worst Man, Yet in Paradise
lineage.i.asiyaContrast.label: Asiya was married to Pharaoh — the most tyrannical figure in the Quran who claimed to be god. Yet her own faith made her one of the greatest believers. The Quran deliberately pairs her story with the wives of Nuh and Lut: closeness to the worst did not corrupt her.
lineage.i.believingManPharaoh.title: The Believing Man in Pharaoh's Court
lineage.i.believingManPharaoh.label: A man from Pharaoh's own family and inner circle hid his faith and spoke up for Musa, reasoning with Pharaoh's people. Living at the centre of the most powerful disbeliever did not prevent him from recognising and protecting the truth.
lineage.i.noBearer.title: No Soul Bears Another's Burden
lineage.i.noBearer.label: The Quran states the principle four times in different surahs: no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Every soul is accountable only for what it earned. No prophet, parent, or ancestor can carry the weight of another person's choices.
lineage.i.fleeFamily.title: On That Day — People Will Flee From Their Own Family
lineage.i.fleeFamily.label: The Quran describes a Day so severe that a man will flee from his own brother, mother, father, wife, and children — every person consumed with their own account. On that Day, the only thing that matters is what a person brought for themselves.
book.title: The Book of Allah — The Quran Describes Itself
book.subtitle: What the Quran says about itself — its names, its purpose, how it was revealed, its challenge to mankind, and its effect on the human heart.
book.sourceNote: All references are drawn directly from Quran ayahs. The Quran's self-descriptions are shown verbatim — no external commentary is added.
book.i.alHuda.title: Al-Huda — The Guidance
book.i.alHuda.label: The Quran calls itself Al-Huda — guidance for those who have taqwa and for all mankind. Its primary purpose, stated in its second verse, is to guide.
book.i.alFurqan.title: Al-Furqan — The Criterion
book.i.alFurqan.label: The Quran calls itself Al-Furqan — the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood. Surah Al-Furqan opens: 'Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant.'
book.i.alNoor.title: Al-Noor — The Light
book.i.alNoor.label: The Quran describes itself as a clear light from Allah that leads people out of darkness into light, by His permission, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
book.i.alShifa.title: Al-Shifa — The Healing
book.i.alShifa.label: The Quran declares itself a healing for what is in the chests — a mercy for the believers. It heals doubts, diseases of the heart, and spiritual ailments.
book.i.alDhikr.title: Al-Dhikr — The Reminder
book.i.alDhikr.label: The Quran calls itself Al-Dhikr — the Reminder. In the same verse Allah declares: 'And indeed it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian.'
book.i.alMubeen.title: Al-Kitab Al-Mubeen — The Clear Book
book.i.alMubeen.label: The Quran opens multiple surahs with the declaration: 'By the Clear Book.' Al-Mubeen means clear, manifest, and making clear — both in itself and in what it clarifies for others.
book.i.alAzeemMajid.title: Al-Azeem & Al-Majid — The Magnificent, The Glorious
book.i.alAzeemMajid.label: Allah describes the Quran as Al-Azeem (Magnificent — 15:87) and Al-Majid (Glorious — 85:21). These are among the greatest titles of honour used for any of Allah's creations.
book.i.alHakim.title: Al-Kitab Al-Hakim — The Book of Wisdom
book.i.alHakim.label: The Quran is called Al-Hakim — the Wise Book, full of wisdom. Surah Ya-Sin opens: 'By the Quran, full of wisdom.' The wisdom it contains is from Allah, the All-Wise.
book.i.guidanceForMankind.title: Guidance for All Mankind
book.i.guidanceForMankind.label: The Quran was sent as guidance for all mankind. Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185) states it was sent as guidance for people, with clear proofs of guidance and the criterion.
book.i.confirmsPrevious.title: Confirms and Guards Previous Scriptures
book.i.confirmsPrevious.label: The Quran states it confirms the Tawrat and the Injil and stands as a guardian over all previous scriptures. It did not come to replace truth — it came to complete and protect it.
book.i.warnerGivesGladTidings.title: Warner and Giver of Glad Tidings
book.i.warnerGivesGladTidings.label: The Quran describes itself as guiding to what is most upright — giving glad tidings to the believers who do good, and warning those who say Allah has taken a son.
book.i.revealedGradually.title: Why Revealed Gradually Over 23 Years
book.i.revealedGradually.label: When disbelievers asked why it was not revealed all at once, the Quran answered: 'So that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have spaced it distinctly.' It came in stages matched to events.
book.i.revealedInArabic.title: Why Revealed in Arabic
book.i.revealedInArabic.label: The Quran explains it was revealed in clear Arabic so that people may understand and reflect. It is from the Lord of all worlds, brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit upon the Prophet's heart.
book.i.laylatalQadr.title: Revealed on Laylat al-Qadr
book.i.laylatalQadr.label: The Quran describes its own night of descent — Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree), better than a thousand months. On that blessed night, the angels and the Spirit descend by Allah's permission.
book.i.tahaddi.title: The Tahaddi — Bring One Surah Like It
book.i.tahaddi.label: The Quran issues a standing challenge: call all your witnesses besides Allah and produce one surah like it — if you are truthful. Mankind and jinn together cannot. If you cannot, and you never will, then fear the Fire.
book.i.protected.title: Allah Guarantees Its Preservation
book.i.protected.label: Allah declares: 'Indeed it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian.' Falsehood cannot approach the Quran from before it or behind it — a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.
book.i.mountainHumbles.title: A Mountain Would Humble Itself
book.i.mountainHumbles.label: Allah says: had We sent down this Quran on a mountain, you would have seen it humbling itself and splitting apart from fear of Allah. These are examples Allah presents so that people may reflect.
book.i.skinsHeartsHumble.title: Skins and Hearts Soften
book.i.skinsHeartsHumble.label: Allah describes the Quran: 'The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it, then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah.' It acts on both the body and the soul.
book.i.increasesIman.title: Increases the Believers in Iman
book.i.increasesIman.label: The Quran states that when its verses are recited, true believers increase in faith. Surah At-Tawbah asks: 'As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith.'
sabr.title: Sabr & Shukr — Patience & Gratitude
sabr.subtitle: Quranic references on patience (Sabr) and gratitude (Shukr) — types, rewards, prophets' examples, and gratitude to Allah.
sabr.sourceNote: Sabr and Shukr references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. No generated religious advice.
sabr.i.sabrWithPrayer.title: Seek Help Through Patience and Prayer
sabr.i.sabrWithPrayer.label: The Quran commands seeking help through sabr and salah — patience is linked directly to worship.
sabr.i.beautifulPatience.title: Beautiful Patience (Sabrun Jameel)
sabr.i.beautifulPatience.label: Yaqub demonstrated Sabrun Jameel — a patience that doesn't complain to creation, only to Allah.
sabr.i.sabrOnTrials.title: Patience Under Trials
sabr.i.sabrOnTrials.label: The Quran promises that those who are patient during loss and hardship receive blessings and mercy from Allah.
sabr.i.allahWithPatient.title: Allah is With the Patient
sabr.i.allahWithPatient.label: The Quran repeatedly declares: 'Verily, Allah is with the patient.'
sabr.i.rewardWithoutAccount.title: Reward Without Measure
sabr.i.rewardWithoutAccount.label: The Quran promises that the patient will receive their reward without account or limit.
sabr.i.shukrIncrease.title: If You Are Grateful, I Will Increase You
sabr.i.shukrIncrease.label: The most famous gratitude verse: Allah promises to increase the one who is grateful and warns of punishment for ingratitude.
sabr.i.shukrToParents.title: Gratitude to Allah and Parents Together
sabr.i.shukrToParents.label: The Quran links gratitude to Allah directly with gratitude and kindness to parents.
sabr.i.shukrOrKufr.title: Gratitude or Ingratitude — A Choice
sabr.i.shukrOrKufr.label: The Quran frames shukr as a deliberate choice; ingratitude is framed as a form of rejection.
sabr.i.ayyubPatience.title: Ayyub's Patience in Suffering
sabr.i.ayyubPatience.label: Ayyub called upon Allah in his suffering without despairing; Allah relieved him and restored him.
sabr.i.yaqubPatience.title: Yaqub's Patience Over Yusuf
sabr.i.yaqubPatience.label: Yaqub kept his grief between himself and Allah, demonstrating that sabr is not absence of feeling.
sabr.i.nuhPatience.title: Nuh's Patience Over 950 Years
sabr.i.nuhPatience.label: The Quran describes Nuh calling his people for 950 years — the longest recorded act of patient perseverance.
knowledge.title: Knowledge & Wisdom
knowledge.subtitle: Quranic references on seeking knowledge, wisdom (Hikmah), the pen, scholars, and the prohibition of following conjecture.
knowledge.sourceNote: Knowledge and wisdom references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. No generated scholarly opinion.
knowledge.i.iqra.title: Iqra — The First Revelation
knowledge.i.iqra.label: The very first words revealed to the Prophet were a command to read, in the name of Allah who taught by the pen.
knowledge.i.taughtByPen.title: Allah Taught by the Pen
knowledge.i.taughtByPen.label: The Quran establishes that Allah taught what humans did not know — through the pen and through revelation.
knowledge.i.increaseKnowledge.title: Dua: My Lord, Increase Me in Knowledge
knowledge.i.increaseKnowledge.label: The Quran records a direct command to ask Allah for increase in knowledge — the only such dua for a personal increase.
knowledge.i.knowDontKnow.title: Are Those Who Know Equal to Those Who Don't?
knowledge.i.knowDontKnow.label: The Quran asks rhetorically whether those who know and those who don't are equal — and answers clearly that they are not.
knowledge.i.fearFromKnowledge.title: Only Those with Knowledge Truly Fear Allah
knowledge.i.fearFromKnowledge.label: The Quran states that among Allah's servants, only those with knowledge (ulema) truly fear Him.
knowledge.i.askPeopleOfKnowledge.title: Ask the People of Knowledge
knowledge.i.askPeopleOfKnowledge.label: The Quran commands those who don't know to ask the people of knowledge.
knowledge.i.wisdomGiven.title: Wisdom is a Great Gift
knowledge.i.wisdomGiven.label: The Quran describes Hikmah (wisdom) as a vast good given by Allah to whom He wills.
knowledge.i.luqmanWisdom.title: Luqman's Wisdom
knowledge.i.luqmanWisdom.label: The Quran preserves Luqman's wisdom — gratitude to Allah, avoiding shirk, honoring parents, not being arrogant.
knowledge.i.unseen.title: The Keys of the Unseen
knowledge.i.unseen.label: The Quran distinguishes between what humans can know and what only Allah knows — the boundaries of human knowledge.
knowledge.i.forbiddenConjecture.title: Following Conjecture is Forbidden
knowledge.i.forbiddenConjecture.label: The Quran warns strongly against following Zann (conjecture) in matters of religion — only verified knowledge is acceptable.
knowledge.i.writingContract.title: The Longest Verse: Write Your Contracts
knowledge.i.writingContract.label: The Quran's longest single verse commands writing contracts and debts as an act of justice and responsibility.
jinn.title: Jinn & Shaytan
jinn.subtitle: Quranic accounts of the jinn, Iblis's refusal, Shaytan's enmity, and protection from his deception.
jinn.sourceNote: All accounts are drawn directly from Quran ayahs. References to hadith on jinn are excluded.
angels.title: Angels in the Quran
angels.subtitle: Quranic descriptions of the angels — their nature, named angels, their roles, and their relationship with humanity.
angels.sourceNote: Only Quran-stated attributes and roles are included. Hadith-only accounts are not listed.
heart.title: The Heart in the Quran
heart.subtitle: Quranic verses on the states of the human heart — sealed hearts, purified hearts, hearts that remember, and hearts that disease takes hold of.
heart.sourceNote: Verses are shown verbatim from the Quran. The heart (qalb) is the spiritual centre in Quranic language.
death.title: Death & Barzakh
death.subtitle: Quranic verses on the certainty of death, the taking of the soul, the Barzakh, martyrs, and the return to Allah.
death.sourceNote: Topics are drawn from direct Quran ayahs only. Details from hadith on the grave are not included here.
yusuf.title: Story of Yusuf
yusuf.subtitle: The complete Quranic narrative of Prophet Yusuf — betrayal, trials, patience, and rise to honour. The Quran calls it 'the best of stories.'
yusuf.sourceNote: The story is recounted almost entirely in Surah Yusuf (12). Passages are shown verbatim from the Quran.
musa.title: Story of Musa
musa.subtitle: The Quranic account of Prophet Musa — from his birth to confronting Pharaoh, the Exodus, and the covenant at Sinai.
musa.sourceNote: Events are drawn from multiple Quranic surahs. Verses are shown verbatim; details vary across the retellings in the Quran.
ibrahim.title: Story of Ibrahim
ibrahim.subtitle: The Quranic account of Ibrahim — the father of monotheism — from his call against idols to building the Kaaba and his legacy as a Hanif.
ibrahim.sourceNote: Ibrahim's story appears across many surahs. Passages are shown verbatim from the Quran.
cave.title: People of the Cave
cave.subtitle: The Quranic story of the youth who fled to a cave for their faith, along with the other great stories of Surah Al-Kahf.
cave.sourceNote: All stories are from Surah Al-Kahf (18). Passages are shown verbatim.
modesty.title: Modesty & Hijab
modesty.subtitle: Quranic guidance on lowering the gaze, modest dress, chaste conduct, and family privacy rules.
modesty.sourceNote: Rulings are drawn directly from Quran ayahs. Fiqh derivations and scholarly opinions on dress codes are not listed.
arrogance.title: Arrogance & Pride
arrogance.subtitle: Quranic warnings against kibr (arrogance) — from Iblis to Pharaoh to Qaroon — and the Quranic call to humility.
arrogance.sourceNote: All references are drawn from Quran ayahs. The term kibr covers both arrogance and pride in Quranic usage.
backbiting.title: Backbiting & Slander
backbiting.subtitle: Quranic warnings against gheebah (backbiting), slander, mockery, suspicion, and false accusation.
backbiting.sourceNote: All references are from Quran ayahs. The vivid comparison in 49:12 is among the Quran's strongest social prohibitions.
tawakkul.title: Tawakkul — Trust in Allah
tawakkul.subtitle: Quranic references on relying upon Allah — His promise to the trusting, prophets' reliance, and Tawakkul with action.
tawakkul.sourceNote: Tawakkul references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. No generated religious advice.
tawakkul.i.allahuWakeel.title: Allah is Sufficient as Wakeel
tawakkul.i.allahuWakeel.label: The Quran describes those who say 'Allah is sufficient for us' when threatened — and are rewarded.
tawakkul.i.whoeverTrusts.title: Whoever Relies on Allah — He is Sufficient
tawakkul.i.whoeverTrusts.label: The most cited Tawakkul verse: whoever puts trust in Allah, He is sufficient for him.
tawakkul.i.birdsExample.title: Birds Trusting in Allah's Provision
tawakkul.i.birdsExample.label: The Quran describes birds setting out in the morning trusting in Allah — and returning full.
tawakkul.i.ibrahimFamily.title: Ibrahim's Reliance Leaving His Family
tawakkul.i.ibrahimFamily.label: Ibrahim left his family in a barren valley relying entirely on Allah to provide for them.
tawakkul.i.musaTrustsAllah.title: Musa's Reliance in Front of Pharaoh
tawakkul.i.musaTrustsAllah.label: Musa declared his reliance on Allah even when cornered between the sea and Pharaoh's army.
tawakkul.i.hudReliance.title: Hud's Declaration of Reliance
tawakkul.i.hudReliance.label: Hud declared: 'I put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord.'
tawakkul.i.nuhReliance.title: Nuh's Reliance and Firm Decision
tawakkul.i.nuhReliance.label: Nuh declared complete reliance on Allah and refused to be shaken by his people.
tawakkul.i.makeDecision.title: Consult, Decide, Then Trust Allah
tawakkul.i.makeDecision.label: The Quran instructs: consult, decide, then rely on Allah — Tawakkul comes after effort.
tawakkul.i.dontSlacken.title: Don't Slacken — Trust and Act
tawakkul.i.dontSlacken.label: The Quran forbids weakness or slackening while commanding trust in Allah alongside action.
tawakkul.i.duaOfProphet.title: The Prophet's Dua of Reliance
tawakkul.i.duaOfProphet.label: Quranic duas of prophets placing all reliance on Allah alone.
worship.i.tahajjud.title: The Night Prayer (Tahajjud)
worship.i.tahajjud.label: The Quran commands the Prophet to rise at night for extra prayer and praises those who forsake their beds in devotion.
worship.i.khushu.title: Humility and Presence in Prayer (Khushu)
worship.i.khushu.label: The Quran declares that the believers who are humble in their prayer have attained success.
worship.i.laylatAlQadr.title: Laylat al-Qadr — The Night of Decree
worship.i.laylatAlQadr.label: The Quran declares Laylat al-Qadr better than a thousand months; during it the angels descend by Allah's permission.
worship.i.itikaaf.title: I'tikaf — Seclusion in the Mosque
worship.i.itikaaf.label: The Quran mentions staying in the mosque for worship; the Sacred Mosque is designated for purification and devotion.
worship.i.prayerTimes.title: Times of Prayer
worship.i.prayerTimes.label: The Quran mentions specific times — morning, midday, afternoon, evening, and night — as times of glorification and prayer.
doj.i.deathCertain.title: Every Soul Shall Taste Death
doj.i.deathCertain.label: The Quran declares that every soul will taste death, and on the Day of Judgment their full recompense will be given.
doj.i.timeFixed.title: The Hour of Death is Fixed
doj.i.timeFixed.label: The Quran states that every community and every person has a fixed term that cannot be advanced or delayed.
doj.i.barzakh.title: The Barzakh — A Barrier Until Resurrection
doj.i.barzakh.label: The Quran describes a barrier between death and resurrection through which no soul can return, and in which Pharaoh's people are shown the Fire.
doj.i.martyrsAlive.title: Martyrs Are Alive, Not Dead
doj.i.martyrsAlive.label: The Quran commands not to say that those killed in the path of Allah are dead — they are alive, provided for by their Lord.
social.i.neighbourRights.title: Rights of Neighbours
social.i.neighbourRights.label: The Quran commands ihsan (goodness) to the near neighbour, the far neighbour, and the companion at one's side.
social.i.trustsAmanah.title: Render Trusts to Their Owners
social.i.trustsAmanah.label: The Quran commands rendering trusts to those they belong to and commands judging between people with justice.
social.i.reconcile.title: Reconcile Between Believers
social.i.reconcile.label: The Quran commands believers to make reconciliation between disputing parties, as believers are a brotherhood.
signs.i.humanDesignSign.title: Signs Within Yourselves
signs.i.humanDesignSign.label: The Quran declares that signs are within the human being itself, and that humans were created in the finest form.
signs.i.khalifaEarth.title: Humanity as Stewards of the Earth
signs.i.khalifaEarth.label: The Quran declares that Allah made humanity successors on the earth, entrusted with responsibility over it.
signs.i.doNotCorrupt.title: Do Not Spread Corruption on Earth
signs.i.doNotCorrupt.label: The Quran forbids spreading corruption on the earth after it has been set in order.
signs.i.diversitySign.title: Diversity of Languages and Colours
signs.i.diversitySign.label: The Quran presents the diversity of human languages and colors as a sign of Allah for those who have knowledge.
sabr.i.doNotWeaken.title: Do Not Weaken or Grieve
sabr.i.doNotWeaken.label: The Quran commands the believers not to weaken or grieve, for they are the superior ones if they are truly believers.
sabr.i.afterDifficultyEase.title: With Difficulty Comes Ease
sabr.i.afterDifficultyEase.label: The Quran twice affirms that with every hardship comes ease, and that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
sabr.i.dontDespairAllah.title: Do Not Despair of Allah's Comfort
sabr.i.dontDespairAllah.label: The Quran assures that Allah has not abandoned the Prophet, and commands believers not to despair of Allah's mercy.
sabr.i.complaintToAllah.title: Turning Grief to Allah Alone
sabr.i.complaintToAllah.label: Yaqub said he complained only to Allah about his grief; Ayyub turned to Allah in his suffering rather than despairing.
jinn.i.jinnCreatedFire.title: Jinn Created from Fire
jinn.i.jinnCreatedFire.label: The Quran states that jinn were created from fire, in contrast to humans created from clay.
jinn.i.jinnAndHumans.title: Jinn and Humans Together
jinn.i.jinnAndHumans.label: The Quran addresses jinn and humans together as beings created to worship Allah and held accountable.
jinn.i.iblisRefusal.title: Iblis's Refusal to Prostrate
jinn.i.iblisRefusal.label: The Quran recounts that Iblis refused to bow to Adam, citing his own origin from fire as superior.
jinn.i.iblisRespite.title: Iblis Asked for Respite
jinn.i.iblisRespite.label: The Quran states that Iblis asked Allah for respite until the Day of Resurrection, which was granted.
jinn.i.shaytanVow.title: Shaytan's Vow to Mislead
jinn.i.shaytanVow.label: The Quran records Shaytan's oath to approach humanity from every direction to lead them astray, except Allah's sincere servants.
jinn.i.shaytanOpenEnemy.title: Shaytan is an Open Enemy
jinn.i.shaytanOpenEnemy.label: The Quran repeatedly declares Shaytan to be a clear and open enemy to the children of Adam.
jinn.i.shaytanNoPower.title: Shaytan Has No Power Over Sincere Believers
jinn.i.shaytanNoPower.label: The Quran states that Shaytan has no authority over those who sincerely believe and trust in Allah.
jinn.i.shaytanWhispers.title: Shaytan Whispers
jinn.i.shaytanWhispers.label: The Quran describes Shaytan whispering to Adam and Eve in the garden, and whispering into the hearts of people.
jinn.i.shaytanBeautifiesEvil.title: Shaytan Beautifies Evil Deeds
jinn.i.shaytanBeautifiesEvil.label: The Quran states that Shaytan made evil deeds appear beautiful to those who went astray.
jinn.i.seekRefuge.title: Seek Refuge in Allah
jinn.i.seekRefuge.label: The Quran commands believers to seek refuge in Allah when prompted by Shaytan, as He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
jinn.i.jinnListened.title: The Jinn Who Listened to the Quran
jinn.i.jinnListened.label: The Quran recounts that a group of jinn listened to the recitation of the Quran and believed, marveling at its guidance.
jinn.i.jinnSubmitted.title: Jinn Who Submitted
jinn.i.jinnSubmitted.label: The Quran records believing jinn declaring their submission to Allah and calling their people to accept guidance.
jinn.i.shaytanJudgmentDay.title: Shaytan Disowns His Followers on Judgment Day
jinn.i.shaytanJudgmentDay.label: The Quran records Shaytan addressing his followers on Judgment Day, declaring he had no power over them and disowning them.
angels.i.angelsObeyAllah.title: Angels Do Not Disobey Allah
angels.i.angelsObeyAllah.label: The Quran states that angels do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, executing all that they are ordered.
angels.i.angelsWorshipConstantly.title: Angels Worship Allah Constantly
angels.i.angelsWorshipConstantly.label: The Quran describes angels standing in rows and glorifying Allah, never growing weary or arrogant.
angels.i.jibreelTrustworthy.title: Jibreel — the Trustworthy Spirit
angels.i.jibreelTrustworthy.label: The Quran identifies Jibreel as the faithful spirit who brought down the revelation to the Prophet's heart, possessing great power.
angels.i.mikailMentioned.title: Mikail — Mentioned by Name
angels.i.mikailMentioned.label: The Quran mentions Mikail by name alongside Jibreel, stating that whoever is an enemy to these angels is an enemy of Allah.
angels.i.angelsWithRevelation.title: Angels Descend with the Revelation
angels.i.angelsWithRevelation.label: The Quran states that on the Night of Decree angels and the spirit descend, and that the trustworthy spirit brought down the message.
angels.i.recordingAngels.title: Recording Angels
angels.i.recordingAngels.label: The Quran states that two angels record every word a person utters, and that every soul has a guardian over it.
angels.i.angelOfDeath.title: Angel of Death
angels.i.angelOfDeath.label: The Quran states that the angel of death appointed over people takes their souls at the decreed time.
angels.i.guardianAngels.title: Guardian Angels
angels.i.guardianAngels.label: The Quran describes angels appointed over people as successors who guard them at Allah's command.
angels.i.angelsAtBadr.title: Angels at Badr
angels.i.angelsAtBadr.label: The Quran states that Allah reinforced the believers at Badr with thousands of angels and cast terror into the disbelievers' hearts.
angels.i.angelsAtTheHour.title: Angels at the Hour
angels.i.angelsAtTheHour.label: The Quran describes angels bearing the throne of Allah, surrounding it, and the trumpet being blown by the appointed angel.
angels.i.angelsPrayForBelievers.title: Angels Pray for Believers
angels.i.angelsPrayForBelievers.label: The Quran states that Allah and His angels bestow blessings on the believers, and that the angels bearing the throne ask forgiveness for those who believe.
angels.i.angelsInParadise.title: Angels in Paradise
angels.i.angelsInParadise.label: The Quran describes angels entering upon the inhabitants of Paradise from every gate, greeting them with peace.
heart.i.soundHeart.title: The Sound Heart
heart.i.soundHeart.label: The Quran states that only one who comes to Allah with a sound, pure heart will benefit on the Day of Resurrection.
heart.i.heartsRemember.title: Hearts That Remember
heart.i.heartsRemember.label: The Quran declares that it is in the remembrance of Allah that hearts find tranquility and rest.
heart.i.allahKnowsHearts.title: Allah Knows What Is in the Hearts
heart.i.allahKnowsHearts.label: The Quran repeatedly states that Allah knows what is hidden in the hearts and what the chests conceal.
heart.i.sealedHearts.title: Sealed Hearts
heart.i.sealedHearts.label: The Quran describes Allah sealing the hearts of disbelievers so they cannot understand, as a consequence of their rejection.
heart.i.hardenedHearts.title: Hardened Hearts
heart.i.hardenedHearts.label: The Quran compares hard hearts to stone or harder still, and warns that those whose hearts are hardened are in clear misguidance.
heart.i.heartsVeiled.title: Hearts Veiled from Truth
heart.i.heartsVeiled.label: The Quran states that coverings are placed over the hearts of those who reject, preventing them from understanding the Quran.
heart.i.diseaseInHeart.title: Disease in the Heart
heart.i.diseaseInHeart.label: The Quran describes hypocrisy and doubt as a disease in the heart, which Allah increases for those who persist in it.
heart.i.tranquilityDescends.title: Tranquility Descends on the Heart
heart.i.tranquilityDescends.label: The Quran states that Allah sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers to increase them in faith.
heart.i.heartsAtMention.title: Hearts Tremble at the Mention of Allah
heart.i.heartsAtMention.label: The Quran describes the true believers as those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned and whose faith increases when His verses are recited.
heart.i.fearAndHope.title: Fear and Hope in the Heart
heart.i.fearAndHope.label: The Quran describes the hearts of the devout as combining fear and longing, causing them to rise from sleep to worship.
heart.i.turningHearts.title: Turning of Hearts
heart.i.turningHearts.label: The Quran records a prayer asking Allah not to let hearts deviate after guidance, and states that Allah intervenes between a person and their heart.
heart.i.blindHearts.title: Blind Hearts
heart.i.blindHearts.label: The Quran states that it is not the eyes that are blind but the hearts within the chests, and questions why they do not reflect on the Quran.
death.i.everySoulTastesDeath.title: Every Soul Shall Taste Death
death.i.everySoulTastesDeath.label: The Quran declares that every soul shall taste death, and that every created thing is destined to perish.
death.i.timeOfDeathFixed.title: The Time of Death is Fixed
death.i.timeOfDeathFixed.label: The Quran states that every community and every individual has an appointed term that cannot be advanced or delayed.
death.i.soulTakenByAngel.title: The Soul Is Taken by the Angel
death.i.soulTakenByAngel.label: The Quran states that the angel of death and his appointed angels take souls at the decreed time.
death.i.sleepMinorDeath.title: Sleep Is the Minor Death
death.i.sleepMinorDeath.label: The Quran states that Allah takes souls at the time of death and during sleep, returning those not decreed to die until their appointed term.
death.i.barzakhBarrier.title: The Barzakh — A Barrier Until Resurrection
death.i.barzakhBarrier.label: The Quran states that behind the deceased is a barzakh until the day they are resurrected, when the horn is blown and they rise from their resting places.
death.i.martyrsAlive.title: Martyrs Are Alive, Not Dead
death.i.martyrsAlive.label: The Quran instructs not to say that those killed in Allah's path are dead, for they are alive with their Lord, rejoicing in His bounty.
death.i.momentOfDeath.title: The Moment of Death
death.i.momentOfDeath.label: The Quran describes the soul reaching the collarbone and the gaze fixing upward at the moment of death, when it is too late to repent.
death.i.returnToAllah.title: Return to Allah
death.i.returnToAllah.label: The Quran teaches that believers say they belong to Allah and to Him they return, and that all will return to Him on the Day of Reckoning.
death.i.goodEndBadEnd.title: Good End Versus Bad End
death.i.goodEndBadEnd.label: The Quran contrasts the angels who take the righteous souls in goodness with those who take the souls of wrongdoers while they are in sin.
death.i.deathCannotBeEscaped.title: Death Cannot Be Escaped
death.i.deathCannotBeEscaped.label: The Quran states that death will overtake you wherever you are, even in lofty towers, and that fleeing from it is futile.
death.i.stateInGrave.title: The State in the Grave
death.i.stateInGrave.label: The Quran describes Pharaoh's people being exposed to the Fire morning and evening in the barzakh before the final Hour.
death.i.givingAccount.title: Giving Account After Death
death.i.givingAccount.label: The Quran describes the disbelievers acknowledging in the afterlife that they have died twice and been given life twice, admitting their sins.
yusuf.i.yusufDream.title: Yusuf's Dream
yusuf.i.yusufDream.label: The Quran recounts Yusuf seeing eleven stars, the sun, and the moon prostrating to him, which his father Ya'qub interpreted as a sign of prophethood.
yusuf.i.brothersJealousy.title: Brothers' Jealousy
yusuf.i.brothersJealousy.label: The Quran describes how Yusuf's brothers envied him for being more beloved to their father and plotted to remove him.
yusuf.i.thrownInWell.title: Thrown in the Well
yusuf.i.thrownInWell.label: The Quran states that Yusuf's brothers threw him in the well, and he was later found and sold for a cheap price by a passing caravan.
yusuf.i.yusufInEgypt.title: Yusuf in the House of Al-Aziz
yusuf.i.yusufInEgypt.label: The Quran states that the man who bought Yusuf in Egypt treated him well, and Allah established Yusuf and gave him knowledge and wisdom.
yusuf.i.seductionAccusation.title: The Seduction and Accusation
yusuf.i.seductionAccusation.label: The Quran recounts that the wife of Al-Aziz sought to seduce Yusuf, who refused, and her plot was exposed when his shirt was torn from behind.
yusuf.i.banquetWomen.title: The Banquet of the Women
yusuf.i.banquetWomen.label: The Quran describes how women who heard of the incident were invited and, upon seeing Yusuf's beauty, cut their hands in astonishment.
yusuf.i.yusufPrefersPrison.title: Yusuf Prefers Prison
yusuf.i.yusufPrefersPrison.label: The Quran records Yusuf praying to Allah to prefer prison over yielding to sin, and Allah answered his prayer.
yusuf.i.dreamsInPrison.title: Dreams in Prison
yusuf.i.dreamsInPrison.label: The Quran recounts two companions in prison sharing their dreams with Yusuf, who interpreted them accurately through Allah's knowledge.
yusuf.i.kingDream.title: The King's Dream
yusuf.i.kingDream.label: The Quran describes the king of Egypt seeing seven fat cows devoured by seven lean ones, which Yusuf alone interpreted as years of plenty followed by drought.
yusuf.i.yusufExonerated.title: Yusuf's Exoneration
yusuf.i.yusufExonerated.label: The Quran states that the king summoned Yusuf, who refused to leave prison until his innocence was publicly established, which it was.
yusuf.i.brothersComeEgypt.title: The Brothers Come to Egypt
yusuf.i.brothersComeEgypt.label: The Quran recounts the brothers of Yusuf coming to Egypt to seek provisions, not recognizing him as the minister who received them.
yusuf.i.reunificationProstration.title: Reunification and Prostration
yusuf.i.reunificationProstration.label: The Quran recounts the fulfillment of Yusuf's childhood dream when his parents and brothers prostrated before him, as he was reunited with his family.
yusuf.i.bestOfStories.title: Best of Stories
yusuf.i.bestOfStories.label: The Quran describes the story of Yusuf as the best of stories and states that in the accounts of the prophets there is a lesson for those of understanding.
yusuf.i.yusufPrayer.title: Yusuf's Prayer
yusuf.i.yusufPrayer.label: The Quran records Yusuf's prayer asking Allah to let him die as a Muslim and join the righteous, after being granted kingdom and knowledge.
musa.i.musaCastInRiver.title: Musa Cast into the River
musa.i.musaCastInRiver.label: The Quran recounts that Allah inspired Musa's mother to place him in the river, promising to return him and make him a messenger.
musa.i.musaInPharaohsHouse.title: Musa in Pharaoh's House
musa.i.musaInPharaohsHouse.label: The Quran states that Pharaoh's household picked up Musa from the river, and Pharaoh's wife urged that they not kill him as he may be of benefit.
musa.i.musaFlees.title: Musa Flees Egypt
musa.i.musaFlees.label: The Quran recounts that Musa accidentally caused the death of a man in a dispute and fled Egypt after being warned of a plot against him.
musa.i.musaInMadyan.title: Musa in Madyan — Marriage
musa.i.musaInMadyan.label: The Quran recounts that Musa helped two women water their flocks in Madyan and later married one of them after completing a term of service.
musa.i.burningBush.title: The Burning Bush — Call to Prophethood
musa.i.burningBush.label: The Quran describes how Allah called to Musa from the sacred valley at the burning bush and appointed him as a messenger to Pharaoh.
musa.i.staffWhiteHand.title: The Staff and the White Hand — Signs
musa.i.staffWhiteHand.label: The Quran records Allah giving Musa two clear signs: his staff becoming a serpent and his hand emerging radiant white.
musa.i.confrontingPharaoh.title: Confronting Pharaoh
musa.i.confrontingPharaoh.label: The Quran recounts Musa and Harun going to Pharaoh to deliver the message and the contest with the sorcerers, whom Musa's staff defeated.
musa.i.plaguesOnEgypt.title: Plagues on Egypt
musa.i.plaguesOnEgypt.label: The Quran states that Allah seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits, and sent plagues as signs, which they still rejected.
musa.i.partingOfSea.title: Parting of the Sea
musa.i.partingOfSea.label: The Quran recounts that Allah commanded Musa to strike the sea with his staff, and it parted as dry paths, saving the Israelites while Pharaoh's army drowned.
musa.i.goldenCalf.title: The Golden Calf
musa.i.goldenCalf.label: The Quran recounts that the Israelites, led astray by al-Samiri, worshipped a golden calf while Musa was away on the mount, angering both Musa and Allah.
musa.i.torahAndTablets.title: The Torah and the Tablets
musa.i.torahAndTablets.label: The Quran states that Allah wrote for Musa on the tablets guidance and detail for all things, and gave the Israelites the Torah as light and guidance.
musa.i.musaAtSinai.title: Musa at Mount Sinai
musa.i.musaAtSinai.label: The Quran recounts that Allah appointed Musa forty nights at the mount where he received the Torah, while the covenant was taken from Bani Isra'il.
musa.i.requestToSeeAllah.title: Request to See Allah
musa.i.requestToSeeAllah.label: The Quran recounts that Musa asked Allah to show Himself, and when Allah's glory was manifested on the mountain it crumbled and Musa fell unconscious.
musa.i.alKhidr.title: Musa and Al-Khidr
musa.i.alKhidr.label: The Quran recounts Musa's journey with a man of special knowledge, who performed three acts that Musa questioned but which each had a divine wisdom.
ibrahim.i.ibrahimQuestionsFather.title: Ibrahim Questions His Father
ibrahim.i.ibrahimQuestionsFather.label: The Quran recounts Ibrahim addressing his father with gentleness, asking why he worships what cannot hear, see, or benefit him.
ibrahim.i.debatingStars.title: Debating the Stars and Heavenly Bodies
ibrahim.i.debatingStars.label: The Quran describes Ibrahim examining the stars, moon, and sun, and rejecting each as a god when they set, declaring he turns solely to the Creator.
ibrahim.i.ibrahimSmashesIdols.title: Ibrahim Smashes the Idols
ibrahim.i.ibrahimSmashesIdols.label: The Quran recounts that Ibrahim broke the idols of his people except the largest, then challenged them to ask their idols who had done it.
ibrahim.i.ibrahimCastIntoFire.title: Ibrahim Cast into the Fire
ibrahim.i.ibrahimCastIntoFire.label: The Quran recounts that Ibrahim's people decided to burn him as punishment for smashing their idols and defying their way.
ibrahim.i.fireBecomesCool.title: The Fire Becomes Cool
ibrahim.i.fireBecomesCool.label: The Quran states that Allah commanded the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim, and their plot against him was foiled.
ibrahim.i.ibrahimMigrates.title: Ibrahim Migrates
ibrahim.i.ibrahimMigrates.label: The Quran states that Ibrahim migrated, declaring he was going toward his Lord, and that Lut believed with him and they journeyed together.
ibrahim.i.ibrahimDuaForMecca.title: Ibrahim's Prayer for Mecca and His Family
ibrahim.i.ibrahimDuaForMecca.label: The Quran records Ibrahim's prayer asking Allah to make Mecca a city of peace, provide its people with fruits, and establish prayer among his descendants.
ibrahim.i.buildingKaaba.title: Building the Kaaba with Isma'il
ibrahim.i.buildingKaaba.label: The Quran states that Ibrahim and Isma'il raised the foundations of the Sacred House, praying that Allah accept it from them and make them submissive.
ibrahim.i.dreamSacrifice.title: The Dream of the Sacrifice
ibrahim.i.dreamSacrifice.label: The Quran recounts that Ibrahim saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son, and when both submitted, Allah ransomed the son with a great sacrifice.
ibrahim.i.ibrahimFriendOfAllah.title: Ibrahim Called the Friend of Allah
ibrahim.i.ibrahimFriendOfAllah.label: The Quran states that Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend, as a result of his complete submission and following the way of monotheism.
ibrahim.i.ibrahimPrayerForProgeny.title: Ibrahim's Prayer for His Progeny
ibrahim.i.ibrahimPrayerForProgeny.label: The Quran records Ibrahim praying that a messenger from among his descendants be raised to teach the scripture and wisdom and purify the people.
ibrahim.i.hanif.title: Hanif — The Pure Monotheist
ibrahim.i.hanif.label: The Quran describes Ibrahim as a hanif, a pure monotheist who was not a polytheist, and calls believers to follow his way.
cave.i.youthsSeekRefuge.title: The Youths Seek Refuge in the Cave
cave.i.youthsSeekRefuge.label: The Quran recounts that the youths of the cave fled to it and prayed to Allah for mercy and right guidance, and He sealed their hearing for years.
cave.i.sleepOfCave.title: The Sleep of the Cave
cave.i.sleepOfCave.label: The Quran states that the sun passed over them without touching them, they appeared awake but slept, and they remained in the cave for three hundred years plus nine.
cave.i.debateOverNumber.title: Debate Over Their Number
cave.i.debateOverNumber.label: The Quran states that people will say the youths were three, or five, or seven, and that the precise count is known only to Allah.
cave.i.theirAwakening.title: Their Awakening
cave.i.theirAwakening.label: The Quran recounts the youths awakening not knowing how long they had slept, sending one to buy food, and their story becoming a sign for the people of the city.
cave.i.twoGardenOwners.title: The Believer and the Disbeliever — Two Garden Owners
cave.i.twoGardenOwners.label: The Quran contrasts a man who was given two gardens and became arrogant, denying resurrection, with his believing companion who warned him; the garden was destroyed.
cave.i.dhulQarnayn.title: The Story of Dhul-Qarnayn
cave.i.dhulQarnayn.label: The Quran recounts that Dhul-Qarnayn traveled to the ends of the earth and built a barrier of iron and copper to hold back Gog and Magog.
cave.i.musaAndKhidr.title: The Story of Musa and Al-Khidr
cave.i.musaAndKhidr.label: The Quran recounts Musa seeking a man of special knowledge at the junction of two seas, who performed three acts each carrying divine wisdom Musa could not perceive.
cave.i.doNotSayTomorrow.title: Do Not Say 'I Will Do This Tomorrow'
cave.i.doNotSayTomorrow.label: The Quran instructs not to say of anything 'I will do it tomorrow' without adding 'if Allah wills,' and to remember your Lord when you forget.
cave.i.tawakkulInCave.title: Tawakkul — Trusting Allah Entirely
cave.i.tawakkulInCave.label: The Quran records the prayer of the cave youths asking Allah for mercy and to arrange their affair rightly, showing complete reliance on Him.
cave.i.worldIsAdornment.title: The World Is Adornment and Fleeting
cave.i.worldIsAdornment.label: The Quran likens the life of this world to rain that causes vegetation to flourish then wither, while righteous deeds are better in reward with your Lord.
cave.i.knowledgeWithAllah.title: Allah's Knowledge Is Infinite
cave.i.knowledgeWithAllah.label: The Quran states that if the sea were ink for the words of Allah, it would be exhausted before His words were, even if an equal sea were added.
cave.i.arroganceDestroyedByTime.title: Arrogance Destroyed by Time
cave.i.arroganceDestroyedByTime.label: The Quran describes how the arrogant garden owner's crops were destroyed overnight, leaving him to say he wished he had not associated anyone with his Lord.
modesty.i.menLowerGaze.title: Men Lower Their Gaze
modesty.i.menLowerGaze.label: The Quran commands believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, stating this is purer for them.
modesty.i.womenLowerGaze.title: Women Lower Their Gaze
modesty.i.womenLowerGaze.label: The Quran commands believing women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, as part of broader modesty requirements.
modesty.i.womenDrawCovers.title: Women Draw Their Covers
modesty.i.womenDrawCovers.label: The Quran instructs women to draw their head coverings over their chests and that the Prophet's wives and believing women draw their outer garments close around them.
modesty.i.jilbabFreeWomen.title: Outer Garment for Believing Women
modesty.i.jilbabFreeWomen.label: The Quran instructs the Prophet to tell believing women to draw their outer garments over themselves so they may be recognized and not harmed.
modesty.i.khimar.title: Khimar — Head Covering
modesty.i.khimar.label: The Quran instructs believing women to draw their head coverings over their chests and not display their adornment except what is apparent.
modesty.i.seekingPermission.title: Seeking Permission Before Entering
modesty.i.seekingPermission.label: The Quran commands believers not to enter homes other than their own without seeking permission and greeting the occupants.
modesty.i.modestWalking.title: Modest Walking
modesty.i.modestWalking.label: The Quran instructs women not to strike their feet to draw attention to their hidden adornment.
modesty.i.modestyInVoice.title: Modesty in Voice
modesty.i.modestyInVoice.label: The Quran instructs the Prophet's wives not to be soft in speech lest those with diseased hearts be tempted, but to speak with appropriate words.
modesty.i.screenAsPrivacy.title: Screen as a Privacy Barrier
modesty.i.screenAsPrivacy.label: The Quran instructs believers to ask the Prophet's wives for things from behind a screen, as that is purer for both parties.
modesty.i.notDisplayingAdornment.title: Not Displaying Adornment
modesty.i.notDisplayingAdornment.label: The Quran instructs believing women not to display their adornment except to specified close relatives, and instructs the Prophet's wives not to make a display of themselves.
modesty.i.garmentOfTaqwa.title: The Garment of Taqwa
modesty.i.garmentOfTaqwa.label: The Quran states that Allah has given garments to cover nakedness and as adornment, but that the garment of God-consciousness is the best.
modesty.i.elderlyWomenPermission.title: Permission for Elderly Women
modesty.i.elderlyWomenPermission.label: The Quran states that elderly women who have passed child-bearing age are not at fault if they lay aside their outer garment without displaying adornment.
modesty.i.modestyCombined.title: Modesty Is Comprehensive
modesty.i.modestyCombined.label: The Quran addresses both men and women with commands covering the gaze, dress, and conduct together as a complete system of modesty.
arrogance.i.doNotWalkProudly.title: Do Not Walk Proudly on the Earth
arrogance.i.doNotWalkProudly.label: The Quran commands not to walk on earth with arrogance, for you cannot split the earth nor reach the mountains in height.
arrogance.i.arrogantNotEnterParadise.tit: The Arrogant Will Not Enter Paradise
arrogance.i.arrogantNotEnterParadise.lab: The Quran states that those who deny Allah's signs and are arrogant will not enter Paradise and will be told to enter the gates of Hell permanently.
arrogance.i.iblisArrogance.title: Iblis's Arrogance — First Act of Kibr
arrogance.i.iblisArrogance.label: The Quran records that Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam, saying he was better because he was created from fire, making him the first to display arrogance.
arrogance.i.pharaohArrogance.title: Pharaoh's Arrogance
arrogance.i.pharaohArrogance.label: The Quran states that Pharaoh and his troops behaved arrogantly without right, and that Pharaoh called out claiming to be his people's highest lord.
arrogance.i.qaroonArrogance.title: Qaroon's Arrogance
arrogance.i.qaroonArrogance.label: The Quran recounts that Qaroon went out to his people in his adornment boasting of his wealth, and was swallowed by the earth as a consequence.
arrogance.i.peopleOfAd.title: The People of 'Ad
arrogance.i.peopleOfAd.label: The Quran recounts that the people of 'Ad said no one was mightier than them in power, then the wind destroyed them because of their arrogance.
arrogance.i.turningAwayInPride.title: Turning Away in Pride
arrogance.i.turningAwayInPride.label: The Quran describes those who hear the signs of Allah and turn away in arrogance as deserving a painful punishment.
arrogance.i.turningFaceInContempt.title: Do Not Turn Face from People in Contempt
arrogance.i.turningFaceInContempt.label: The Quran instructs not to turn your cheek away from people in contempt nor walk in insolence, and to be moderate in walking and lowering the voice.
arrogance.i.allahDoesNotLoveArrogant.tit: Allah Does Not Love the Arrogant
arrogance.i.allahDoesNotLoveArrogant.lab: The Quran clearly states that Allah does not love those who are arrogant and boastful.
arrogance.i.walkingHumbly.title: Walking Humbly on Earth
arrogance.i.walkingHumbly.label: The Quran describes the servants of the Most Merciful as those who walk upon the earth in humility.
arrogance.i.selfPraiseForbidden.title: Self-Praise Forbidden
arrogance.i.selfPraiseForbidden.label: The Quran states not to claim purity for oneself, as Allah knows best who is truly righteous.
arrogance.i.servantsWalkHumbly.title: The Servants of the Most Merciful Walk Humbly
arrogance.i.servantsWalkHumbly.label: The Quran opens its description of the true servants of Allah with their characteristic of walking on the earth with humility.
backbiting.i.backbitingFlesh.title: Backbiting Compared to Eating Flesh
backbiting.i.backbitingFlesh.label: The Quran asks whether anyone would like to eat the flesh of his dead brother, using this as an analogy for backbiting to make its gravity clear.
backbiting.i.avoidSuspicion.title: Avoid Much Suspicion
backbiting.i.avoidSuspicion.label: The Quran instructs believers to avoid much suspicion, as some suspicion is sin, and not to spy on or backbite one another.
backbiting.i.noSpying.title: No Spying
backbiting.i.noSpying.label: The Quran prohibits spying on one another and instructs not to enter private spaces without permission, protecting the privacy of others.
backbiting.i.doNotMock.title: Do Not Mock Each Other
backbiting.i.doNotMock.label: The Quran prohibits believers from mocking other people, as those being mocked may be better than those who mock them.
backbiting.i.doNotCallBadNames.title: Do Not Call Each Other Bad Names
backbiting.i.doNotCallBadNames.label: The Quran instructs believers not to insult each other with offensive nicknames after having accepted faith, calling it wickedness.
backbiting.i.slanderAgainstAisha.title: Slander — Warning to Believers
backbiting.i.slanderAgainstAisha.label: The Quran addresses those who spread slander against a believing woman, calling it a grave sin and warning that those who spread it face a painful punishment.
backbiting.i.spreadingIndecency.title: Those Who Spread Indecency
backbiting.i.spreadingIndecency.label: The Quran warns those who love to see indecency spread among the believers that they will have a painful punishment in this world and the hereafter.
backbiting.i.speakRightly.title: Speak Rightly or Stay Silent
backbiting.i.speakRightly.label: The Quran instructs believers to fear Allah and speak rightly so that He may set their deeds right and forgive their sins.
backbiting.i.accusingChasteWomen.title: Accusing Chaste Women
backbiting.i.accusingChasteWomen.label: The Quran prescribes eighty lashes for those who accuse chaste women without four witnesses, and states that those who accuse chaste believing women are cursed.
backbiting.i.slandererTaleBearer.title: The Slanderer Who Goes About Tale-Bearing
backbiting.i.slandererTaleBearer.label: The Quran condemns those who go about with malicious gossip and slander, warning of destruction for every scorner and slanderer.
backbiting.i.seekingPermissionPrivacy.la: The Quran commands believers not to enter homes other than their own until they have asked permission and greeted the inhabitants.
backbiting.i.forgiveAndOverlook.title: Forgive and Overlook
backbiting.i.forgiveAndOverlook.label: The Quran encourages those of virtue to forgive and overlook rather than retaliate in kind, and asks if they would not love Allah to forgive them.
